title: Global Media Asset Distribution for Streamline Studios
business: Streamline Studios operates a global platform for high-resolution digital media assets, requiring consistent access for creative teams distributed across multiple continents.
problem: The centralized origin server experiences significant latency and connection timeouts when users in distant regions attempt to fetch large media files, leading to workflow bottlenecks.
solution: By implementing a Content Delivery Network, the studio caches static media assets at geographically distributed edge locations, ensuring that users retrieve data from a server physically closer to their location rather than the origin.
steps: Configure the origin server to set appropriate Cache-Control headers for static assets.
Provision a CDN distribution and map it to the origin server's domain.
Update DNS records to point the media subdomain to the CDN's provided edge endpoint.
Validate that subsequent requests for assets are served with cache-hit headers from edge nodes.
outcome: Creative teams experience reduced latency and more reliable download speeds for large assets, as traffic is offloaded from the origin server to the edge network.
limitation: The primary limitation is cache invalidation latency; when an asset is updated at the origin, the edge nodes may continue serving the stale version until the Time-To-Live (TTL) expires or a manual purge is triggered. To check for this, developers can inspect the Age and X-Cache headers in the HTTP response to determine if the content is being served from the edge cache or the origin.
